record.paper_title: Open Problems in Nuclear Density Functional Theory
record.original_question: In a finite harmonic-oscillator shell-model construction, the neutron and proton densities are represented by finite density-polynomial coefficients, the Levy-Lieb density constraints and normalization constraint become algebraic polynomial equations in configuration-mixing coefficients, and eliminating constrained variables and survivor coefficients yields an implicit polynomial relation R(η, Cn1, …, CnNn, Cp1, …, CpNp) = 0 linking the minimal energy η to density parameters. What practical algebraic strategies can handle the resulting large multivariate polynomials, compare distinct polynomial relations R obtained from different finite-basis choices, extrapolate when direct calculations become too cumbersome, and make rigorous polynomial density functionals useful in larger nuclear models?

evidence.quote: One finally obtains a polynomial relation, R(η, Cn1, Cn2, ..., CnNn, Cp1, Cp2, ..., CpNp) = 0, (15) which links the minimal energy to the parameters of ρ. Although not an open formula, this implicit equation, R = 0, has all the needed virtues of a density functional for the calculation of η and its minimization in terms of the density.

It is clear that this rigorous derivation raises several technical problems, such as, for instance, the best tactics to handle big polynomials in the context of many parameters, the comparison of distinct polynomials R obtained from models with different choices for the basis, the search for extrapolations when calculations become too cumbersome. But there is no doubt that this constructive approach offers challenging open problems.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a programmatic open challenge about algebraic-computational strategies (handling, comparing, and extrapolating large implicit polynomial density functionals). No literature was found establishing a general solution; standard tools (Gröbner bases, resultants, numerical algebraic geometry) exist but no rigorous, general framework targeted at this nuclear-density-functional construction has been identified. Status appears open.
